spec.description: Channel settings for one or more broadcasters: what they are streaming or last streamed, under which title, category, language, tags and content labels.

broadcaster_id.description: Broadcaster ids whose channels to read, such as `141981764`. Sent as repeated `broadcaster_id` query parameters; at most 100.

response.title: ChannelsFrame
response.description: The wire frame. `/helix/channels` does not page, so it carries `data` alone.

data.description: The channels found; empty when none of the ids matched.

broadcaster_id.description: An ID that identifies the broadcaster.

broadcaster_language.description: The broadcaster's preferred language, as an ISO 639-1 two-letter code, or `other`.

game_id.description: The category being played or last played; an empty string for a broadcaster that never has.

game_name.description: The name of that category; an empty string for a broadcaster that never played one.

title.description: The title of the current or last broadcast; an empty string for a broadcaster that never streamed.

delay.description: The broadcaster's stream delay setting, in seconds. Zero unless the call used that broadcaster's own user access token and they are a partner who set one.

tags.description: The tags applied to the channel.

content_classification_labels.description: The content classification labels applied to the channel.

is_branded_content.description: Whether the channel is flagged as branded content.

unverified.detail: No recording yet: Helix authenticates every call, and the machine this spec was written on holds no Twitch application credentials. The Record workflow fills this in: it reads the application client id and secret from the repository secrets TWITCH_CLIENT_ID and TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET, mints an app access token through the core, replays this endpoint's `examples/*.request.json` with `truewire capture`, and opens a pull request with the response the API sent.

notes: The response schema is the wire frame, `{"data": [...], "pagination": {...}}`, and no `envelope.payload` is declared, so the method returns the frame and the rows are `result["data"]` (ADR 0010, authoring rule 6). Unwrapping `data` would put the pagination cursor out of reach: pagination paths resolve inside whatever the method returns, and Helix puts the cursor beside `data`, not inside it. One rule for every Helix method is worth more than unwrapping the five endpoints here that never page.

Written from the Helix reference at the `docs` URL above. Fields the reference marks deprecated are not declared; an undeclared field passes validation and is dropped from the validated value, so a recording that carries one is still valid. The first recording confirms or corrects the rest.
